arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Michael McConnell argued the program affects the livelihoods of small California raisin growers.
He stated the case involves important principles and the Hornes' financial survival.
The government attorney argued the program regulates the commercial marketing of a fungible product.
He emphasized the program was established with producer approval for their benefit.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Hornes challenge a federal program that requires them to store part of their raisin crop. They claim this action violates their property rights. The Department of Agriculture defends the program as a cooperative effort. The case tests the limits of government regulation on private property.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between government regulation and property seizure. It determines how much control the state holds over private agricultural assets. The outcome shapes the rights of all small-scale producers.
